$comment: GENERATED by scripts/gen-management-registry.py from sdks/openapi.json. Do not edit by hand -- edit the NAMESPACES table in that script. This file is the input every SDK's §27 code generator reads.

excluded_tags.oauth2: §12 RP helpers, §14 device grant, §15 token exchange, §26 PAR
excluded_tags.uma: §20 UMA 2.0 protection API and ticket grant
excluded_tags.webauthn: §24 WebAuthn ceremonies -- credential I/O, not administration
excluded_tags.federation-sso: §12 public SSO entry points, driven by the RP helpers

excluded_operations.POST /api/v1/organizations: §27.0 boundary -- provisioning an organization is a platform-operator act performed out of band, never from a tenant-scoped SDK client
excluded_operations.DELETE /api/v1/organizations/{org_id}: §27.0 boundary -- destroying an organization destroys every tenant under it; deliberately unreachable from an SDK
excluded_operations.POST /api/v1/admin/bootstrap: §27.0 boundary -- first-run creation of the first organization, tenant and administrator, gated on an out-of-band setup token or environment variable. It is the act that brings a deployment into existence, performed once by a platform operator; there is no tenant-scoped client that could hold the credentials to call it
excluded_operations.POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verificatio: §25 account lifecycle, not §27 management -- this is self-service on the caller's OWN record, the authenticated sibling of the excluded `auth`-tagged POST /auth/resend-verification. §27 is about administering other principals; it is only under the `users` tag because of where the route sits

organizations.doc: Organizations an SDK client may read and configure. Creation and deletion are outside the SDK boundary (§27.0).

tenants.doc: Tenants within an organization -- the isolation boundary every other namespace is scoped to.

users.doc: Users within the client's tenant, and the administrative side of their second factor and lockout state.

groups.doc: Named collections of users. Roles assigned to a group are inherited by every member.

roles.doc: Roles, their permission sets, and their assignment to users and groups.

permissions.doc: Permissions -- an action on a resource, optionally narrowed by a scope.

resources.doc: The resource hierarchy role assignments cascade down.

scopes.doc: Sub-resource granularity, always addressed under their resource.

service_accounts.doc: Machine identities, their secrets, and the certificate a device-bound one authenticates with.

certificates.doc: End-entity X.509 certificates -- the ones issued to users, services and IoT devices.

ca_certificates.doc: Organization CAs and the per-tenant signing CAs chained beneath them.

pgp_keys.doc: OpenPGP keys used for audit signing and encrypted data export.

webhooks.doc: Outbound event notifications. Delivery signatures are verified with the §13 helper, which this namespace configures.

oauth2_clients.doc: Registered OAuth2/OIDC clients -- the registration half of what §12, §21 and §26 then speak to.

federation.doc: Upstream IdP configuration and the per-user links it produces.

notification_rules.doc: Which events raise a notification, and to whom.

email_config.doc: Transactional-mail transport, configurable at organization level and overridable per tenant.

settings.doc: Effective settings, and the organization/tenant layers they resolve from.

scim_tokens.doc: Bearer tokens for the SCIM 2.0 provisioning endpoint.

reactors.doc: Registration of §22 AMQP extension actors -- the admin surface §22.9 describes, which no SDK could previously reach.

webauthn_policy.doc: Per-tenant attestation policy governing the §24 ceremonies, and the compliance report over it.

audit.doc: Append-only audit log, read-only by construction.

privacy.doc: GDPR self-service: the authenticated account's own export and erasure. Scoped to the caller, never to another user.

platform.doc: Deployment-level probes and FIDO metadata state. Unauthenticated where the server leaves them so.

ready.summary: GET /ready` — readiness probe. Checks DB connectivity.
